chapter_scope: v03-c05 and v03-c06 only; remaining six Volume 3 chapters and its assessment/project package remain unfinished
review_type: Author analytic, numerical, source and instructional review; not independent certification

reviewed.reasoning: Reviewed joint-CDF rectangle nonnegativity, marginalization, support restrictions and independence criteria; finite conditioning and conditional moments as random variables; joint-density/conditional-density a.e. qualifications and shrinking-interval regularity; singular continuous joint-law counterexample; total expectation, known-factor rule, nested tower identities, conditional second-moment finiteness, variance/orthogonal forecast-error decomposition and expected information improvement; convolution and independent random sums. Reviewed four convergence definitions/implications/counterexamples, Markov/Chebyshev proofs, finite-variance weak law and integrable truncation proof, maximal inequality plus dyadic Borel–Cantelli proof of the finite-variance strong law. Reviewed complete finite-positive-variance iid CLT via Gaussian convolution, uniform second-order Taylor remainder, one-term independent moment matching, telescoping, finite-second-moment tail split and explicit smooth CDF squeeze. Reviewed Berry–Esseen assumptions as a stated quantitative theorem, covariance-based weak-law conditions, shared-shock limits, moment failures and the stated/proved Slutsky form.
reviewed.arithmetic: Exact joint signal/forecast losses, conditional exercise tables, latent-quality/three-flag enumeration, complete random-sum state distribution, triangular-region independent quadrature for CDFs/marginals/cross-moments/conditional variance, and singular-law generating-variable integrals. Exact rational binomial tails and finite Chebyshev event bounds; corrected and uncorrected normal comparisons; Berry–Esseen input ratio; exhaustive shared-shock average states, typewriter blocks, first-crossing maximal-inequality terms and dyadic geometric tail certificates. Smooth transition derivative/Taylor checks, Gaussian comparison integrals and finite-second/infinite-third-moment density integrals.
reviewed.solutions: All sixteen exercises solved and determinate values independently checked. Convergence and theorem-audit problems have explicit hypotheses, proof or counterexample; finite numerical observations are not treated as proof of asymptotic statements. Studentized-scale solution uses the integrable weak law for squared observations and does not invent independence between sample mean and variance.
reviewed.instruction: Finite tables precede continuous conditioning and conditional expectations as random variables. Zero-point-probability conditioning is distinguished from density-based versions. The CLT proof uses calculus, moment identities, elementary convolution and tail splitting already introduced; no unintroduced characteristic-function continuity theorem or finite-third-moment shortcut is used. General measure construction and the fully integrable strong-law proof remain later foundations/further study and are not claimed to have been proved here.
reviewed.sources: Reused official MIT joint/covariance readings; retrieved method-specific conditional-moment and introductory/statistical limit PDFs plus author-hosted Tao laws/CLT notes. Catalogue records exact URLs and inspection scope. Prose, synthetic examples and exercises are original; classical proof methods are named and further-study sources linked.
reviewed.structure: Each chapter includes two worked examples, eight exercises and complete solutions, boundary/moment/information assumptions, teach-back, delayed checks and method-specific source routes. Integrated structural/source/link/anchor checks are required before acceptance.

corrections: Refined the independent outer quadrature grid after a fourth-degree integrand exceeded the chosen tolerance at the initial coarse grid; no manuscript value was changed by this check.
Specified conditional densities as a.e. versions and gave the exact regularity assumptions for shrinking-interval limits.
Kept the general integrable strong law and quantitative Berry–Esseen theorem explicitly distinct from the versions fully proved here.
limitations: No independent human reviewer or learner trial.
General sigma-algebra conditional-expectation construction remains Chapter 12; the complete general integrable iid strong-law proof requires its own follow-up.
Berry–Esseen is stated with a verified conservative constant and further-study source; its full smoothing/Fourier proof is not presented in this introductory chapter.
All numerical sampling/forecast parameters are stipulated synthetic laws, not fitted population models or observed October data.
Finite calculations and simulations cannot establish general convergence claims; written proofs were audited separately.
Visual/mobile/print UI QA remains pending after the earlier browser-policy rejection.
acceptance: Accepted by the author after completed analytic/solution/source review and successful integrated numerical/structural checks. Remaining Volume 3 chapters/package, the recorded formal-foundations strong-law proof follow-up, independent human validation and visual/mobile/print UI QA remain outstanding.
